paragraphs: Customer Reasons for Managing a Catalog for a Supplier
• They don’t have the technology wherewithal
• They don’t supply enough products for a catalog to make sense
• They provide specialized products or services to that particular customer
• They don’t want to manage the catalog, either because the buyer volume is too low or they think it’s too hard
• The supplier does not maintain catalogs.
• Items provided by the supp lier to that particular buyer are not available in the catalog.
• The customer wants to get a large number of suppliers online very quickly.
• The customer wants to present more information to users than what the supplier provides.
• The customer does not trust supplier to provide correct and up-to-date item detail and pricing or access to only those items that have been negotiated.
• It's the way it's always been done.

paragraphs: Supplier Catalog Managed by Customer in Hosted Catalog
Considerations for Using Hosted Catalogs for Supplier Items
• If the customer uses a hosted catalog to manage the supplier’s catalog, the supplier will not be able to use the JSN portal.
• The supplier will not be able to manage catalogs, contracts, orders, invoices, sourcing events, or run reports in the portal.
• The hosted catalog requires the Default Org Supplier ID.

Price File / Price Set: What’s the Difference?
Price File A file uploaded by the supplier with specific pricing for various clients
• Can include columns for one or multiple clients
• Clients will only see and approve their own (and maybe list) pricing
Price Set The column in that file which designates pricing for a specific client
• From client standpoint, same thing as price file
